title: Effects of the obesity curriculum from the health training programme of the German Federal Pension Insurance in orthopaedic and rheumatological rehabilitation
summary:
Overweight and obesity are highly relevant to health and are also becoming increasingly important as secondary diagnoses in medical rehabilitation. Patient education on nutrition, exercise and behavioral change is part of the basic treatment for obesity and the multimodal rehabilitation program. 
The study examines the effectiveness of a patient education program for rehabilitants with an orthopaedic or rheumatological disease and obesity. Rehabilitants are randomly assigned to the educational group training program or a comparison condition as part of inpatient rehabilitation. Data is collected at the beginning and end of rehabilitation as well as three and six months after completion.
conditions: Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue

interventions.name: Intervention condition: Patient education group program “Curriculum Obesity” from the health training program of the German Federal Pension Insurance. The curriculum is an interactive group program with 5 sessions of 60 minutes each.  It aims to develop participants' knowledge, attitudes, motivation
Control condition: usual care, i.e., a one-hour weight reduction seminar and one-time individual nutritional counseling (if requested by the rehabilitant)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Rehabilitation by the German Pension Insurance 
-informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
-limitations with the German language
-severe impairment of vision or hearing (not corrected)
-serious psychiatric diagnoses (psychosis, personality disorder, dementia)
